questions.q: You forecast 16 days ahead. Which lag is safe for all test days?
why: Correct: lag 16 or more is always in the known history.
Unknown for the last test day.

questions.q: Why build a complete date grid before computing shift features?
options: So that shift(k) means k days even when some dates are missing
To add more rows for the model to learn
why: Grid rows for test days have no target.

questions.q: Why train on y = log1p(sales) with squared error?
options: Its RMSE equals the RMSLE, the competition metric

questions.q: Scenario: validation RMSLE is 0.40 but the public score is 0.85. What do you check first?
options: Leakage in features or a validation that does not copy the test

questions.q: Why is `transactions.csv` hard to use as a feature?
options: It has no rows for the test period
why: Correct: you would need lags of at least 16 days.

questions.q: Which step converts model output back to sales?
why: Correct: expm1 is the inverse of log1p.

questions.q: Scenario: one family has by far the largest error. What is a good next step?
options: Plot its series and check zeros, start dates and promotions; try a separate treatment
why: It may hide a fixable issue.
